document.executive_summary: Round-4 review confirms the client-correct pick: P1. All four packages qualify (quality 98/86/89/100 against the 80 floor; defects 1/5/1/5 against the ceiling of 5) and P1 is the unique lowest-energy qualifier at 6 kWh per acceptance batch, ahead of P3 by 8, P2 by 34 and P4 by 61 kWh. Both delivered documents recomputed this correctly, but each left chart is factually inconsistent with the trusted table: A's bars are drawn off-scale and B's left panel swaps the P2/P3 margins and spare slots. This handover reconciles the verified result, records the figure defects, and lists the sensitivity items and open questions the next analyst must carry forward.
document.figure_caption: Handover diagram: measured energy per acceptance batch on one linear scale (left) beside quality margins and spare defect slots (right); P1 wins on energy, while P2 and P4 carry zero spare defect slots.

recommendation.rationale: P1 is the unique lowest-energy qualifier at 6 kWh per batch — 8 kWh ahead of P3, 34 ahead of P2 and 61 ahead of P4 — with quality 98, one defect and four spare defect slots, and the best energy-per-quality ratio (0.06). Unverified cost or reliability data cannot override the measured energy minimum under the client policy.

sections.body: All four candidates clear the binary screen: quality margins over 80 are 18 (P1), 6 (P2), 9 (P3) and 20 (P4); spare defect slots are 4, 0, 4 and 0. Since qualification is binary and all pass, energy decides. Measured energy per identical acceptance batch ranks P1 6 kWh, P3 14, P2 40 and P4 67. Successive gaps of 8, 26 and 27 kWh and the 61 kWh winner-to-last spread reproduce in both documents, and the energy-per-quality ratios (0.06, 0.16, 0.47, 0.67) also check. Both independent ballots landed on P1, matching the policy's lowest-energy rule; no ID tie-break was needed because the minimum is unique.
sections.heading: Verified Selection Result

sections.body: Both right-hand charts are accurate, but both left charts fail pixel-versus-table verification. In A's brief the left bars are drawn off a single linear scale: P1 (6), P3 (14) and P2 (40) render far taller than the table allows, with P3 nearly as tall as P2, despite A's text claiming a pixel-checked one-scale chart. In B's memo the left panel swaps P2 and P3: it shows P3 with +6 margin and zero spare and P2 with +9 and four spare, inverting the true values (P2 +6/zero spare; P3 +9/four spare), and the low bars are misdrawn. Both prose texts remain correct. Lesson: any drawn value departing from the trusted table is a factual defect, not an open question, and a written pixel-check claim is not verification.
sections.heading: Figure Integrity Findings

sections.body: Two sensitivity facts stand. P2 and P4 sit exactly at the five-defect ceiling with zero spare slots, so one additional measured defect disqualifies either; P1 and P3 tolerate four more. P2 is closest to the quality floor at 86, six points above 80. All energy figures come from one acceptance batch on a shared basis, so batch-to-batch variance is unmeasured. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability remain unverified and cannot move an energy-first ranking. These items are recorded as open questions, not facts, and should be restated as such in the next analyst's brief.
sections.heading: Sensitivity and Open Questions

sections.body: Carry three actions. First, recompute eligibility, gaps and ratios directly from the trusted table before writing; round-4 arithmetic is stable, so the recorded errors are confined to chart rendering. Second, regenerate every chart from the table at one linear scale and pixel-check drawn heights against tabulated values before release, labeling each bar with its table value. Third, carry the open questions — batch variance and unverified cost, delivery, maintenance and reliability — into the round-5 brief without asserting them as facts. The verified selection stands: P1 at 6 kWh, quality 98, one defect, four spare slots.
sections.heading: Handover Actions for the Next Analyst
